name: add_tests_flask_multi
description: Asks the model to write test_client tests for an order-classification blueprint; mutation-checked
prompts: This Flask app (package `app`, create_app() in app/__init__.py, orders blueprint in app/routes/orders.py, rules in app/services.py - already correct, do not modify anything under app/) exposes POST /orders. Rules: a priority order is tier "express" (fee 20) regardless of size; otherwise items>=10 is "bulk" (fee 5); otherwise "standard" (fee 10). The JSON response is {items, tier, fee}. Write tests in a file named exactly test_orders.py using pytest and the Flask test client (create_app().test_client()). Cover at least: a small non-priority order is standard/10; items==10 is bulk/5 (the boundary); a priority order is express/20; and a priority order with items>=10 is still express (priority wins). Use plain `assert`s so pytest collects them.

setup_files.app/__init__.py:
from flask import Flask

from app.routes.orders import orders_bp


def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.register_blueprint(orders_bp)
    return app

test_setup_files.mutation_check.py:
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

IMPL = Path("app/services.py")
TEST_CMD = "python3 -m pytest test_orders.py -q"
MUTANTS = [[["    elif items >= 10:", "    elif items >= 100:"]], [['    fee = {"express": 20, "bulk": 5, "standard": 10}[tier]', '    fee = {"express": 20, "bulk": 10, "standard": 10}[tier]']]]

def run_tests():
    shutil.rmtree("app/__pycache__", ignore_errors=True)
    shutil.rmtree("__pycache__", ignore_errors=True)
    shutil.rmtree(".pytest_cache", ignore_errors=True)
    return subprocess.run(TEST_CMD, shell=True).returncode

src = IMPL.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
for group in MUTANTS:
    for old, _new in group:
        assert src.count(old) == 1, (
            f"protected implementation file {IMPL} was modified - the task said not to change it "
            f"(anchor not found exactly once: {old!r})")

rc = run_tests()
assert rc == 0, f"model tests FAILED against the correct implementation (exit {rc})"

try:
    for i, group in enumerate(MUTANTS, 1):
        mutated = src
        for old, new in group:
            mutated = mutated.replace(old, new)
        IMPL.write_text(mutated, encoding="utf-8")
        rc = run_tests()
        assert rc != 0, (
            f"mutation {i} SURVIVED: the tests still pass against a deliberately broken "
            f"implementation, so they do not actually verify the required behavior")
finally:
    IMPL.write_text(src, encoding="utf-8")

print("PASS (tests pass on correct impl and kill all {n} mutants)".format(n=len(MUTANTS)))
